entities.summary:
Aristides was a renowned Greek musician and composer of the Classical era, active in Thebes during the 5th century BCE. He is known for his contributions to the development of Greek music and his association with the Theban school of music.

Aristides' work had a significant impact on the evolution of Western classical music, influencing later Greek musicians and shaping the development of musical styles in the Mediterranean region. His compositions, which often featured lyre and aulos, were performed at royal courts and public festivals, further solidifying his reputation as a master musician.

The exact dates of Aristides' birth and death are unknown, but his significance as a musician and composer of the Classical era is undeniable. His legacy can be seen in the many musicians who followed in his footsteps, and his contributions to the development of Greek music continue to be celebrated and studied by music historians and enthusiasts alike.

Aristides' association with the Theban school of music, which flourished during the 5th century BCE, is also noteworthy. This school was known for its emphasis on melody and harmony, and Aristides' compositions reflect this focus. His work can be seen as a key example of the artistic and cultural achievements of the Theban school, and his influence can still be felt in the music of the ancient Greek world.
